title: 5 Questions to Ask Before Making Big Decisions
paragraphs: 5 Questions to Ask Before Making Big Decisions
You’re about to make a big decision… and no one sees the battle inside you.

Not the late-night overthinking.
Not the quiet fear of getting it wrong.
But heaven sees it.
And before you move—pause.
Here are 5 questions that could save you from regret… and lead you straight into God’s will:
1. Does this draw me closer to Jesus… or just closer to what I want?

Not everything that feels right is right.
“Follow your heart” sounds good—until your heart leads you away from God.
“The heart is deceitful above all things…” (Jeremiah 17:9)
If it feeds your flesh but starves your spirit—walk away.
2. Am I seeking God… or just asking Him to bless my plan?
There’s a difference.

One is surrender.
The other is control dressed up as prayer.
“Trust in the Lord with all your heart…” (Proverbs 3:5–6)
Don’t move until you’ve truly submitted, not just requested.
3. Do I have peace from the Holy Spirit—or pressure from the world?

God leads with peace.
The world pushes with urgency.
If you feel rushed, anxious, cornered…
That’s not His voice.
“Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts…” (Colossians 3:15)
Peace is your compass.
4. Am I willing to obey… even if it costs me?
This is where many turn back.

We want God’s will—until it requires sacrifice.
But obedience isn’t proven in comfort.
“If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself…” — Jesus Christ (Luke 9:23)
If you’re only saying yes when it’s easy… it’s not surrender yet.
5. If this fails… will I still trust God?
Because sometimes even the right decisions come with hard outcomes.

Faith isn’t “God will make this work.”
Faith is “Even if it doesn’t, He is still good.”
That’s where real trust lives.
But here’s what we miss…

The biggest decision you’ll ever make
is not your career, your relationship, or your next move.
It’s what you do with Jesus.

Because every wrong turn, every regret, every failure—
can be redeemed in Him.

Sin may cloud your judgment.
But grace restores your direction.

At the cross, confusion meets clarity.
At the cross, broken plans meet a perfect Savior.
So before you decide anything… choose Him first.
Then everything else falls into place.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
